title: In which years did the World count at least double?
description: The World line of objects launched into space is read at 2016 and 2017, then at 2019 and 2020. Each reading is compared with twice the earlier one to find the pairs of years where the count at least doubled. The video breaks Keeko's doubt that only the biggest rise counts as doubling.
teaching_notes: One idea: a count has doubled when the later reading is at least twice the earlier one, whatever the size of the rise. Watch for students who pick only the pair with the biggest rise.

source: Use the World line to find two consecutive years where the c
video_script.why: The child can read the World line but has not yet checked whether a later reading is at least twice an earlier one.
video_script.substitution: Read two consecutive years, write twice the earlier reading, and see if the later reading reaches it.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the number of objects launched into space each year
video_script.wrong_answer: only two thousand nineteen to two thousand twenty doubled
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the pair with the biggest rise and ignores that a smaller rise on a small start can also be a doubling.
video_script.payoff_line: it doubled from two thousand sixteen to two thousand seventeen

final_answer.spoken: it doubled from two thousand sixteen to two thousand seventeen, and again from two thousand nineteen to two thousand twenty

maths_rules: World line: 2016 about 230, 2017 about 480, 2019 about 600, 2020 about 1270
twice 230 = 460, and 480 is more than 460; also 480 / 230 is about 2.1
twice 600 = 1200, and 1270 is more than 1200; also 1270 / 600 is about 2.1
rises: 480 - 230 = 250 and 1270 - 600 = 670; the biggest rise is not the only doubling
doubled means the later reading is at least twice the earlier reading
video_script.design: One idea: compare the later reading with twice the earlier one. The wrong idea is that only the biggest rise is a doubling. The World line stays on screen; a ghost dot at twice the earlier height is placed above the earlier dot.

<bookmark mark='test'/>The count has doubled when the later dot reaches twice the height of the earlier dot.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>At least twice means the later dot is at the ghost dot or above it.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only two thousand nineteen to two thousand twenty doubled, because that rise is the biggest.
<bookmark mark='start'/>But doubling depends on where the line started. A small start needs only a small rise to double.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both later dots sit above their ghost dots, so both pairs doubled.
